verdict.reason:
Confirmed on page 9, panel 9.5. In the zoomed crop of the bottom panel (about x 850-1700, y 1880-2520 at full resolution), Varma and Ramayyan sit side by side on two matching high-backed thrones. Both chairs are dark carved wood with finials and red upholstered seats, and both stand at the top of a flight of stone steps. Ramayyan's low table with its palm leaves and ink pot is gone.

The rest of the scene contradicts this:
- **2.2 and 6.1:** Varma sits cross-legged on the low platform. Ramayyan sits at his low table, or cross-legged beside it with leaves.
- **8.5, the panel just before this one:** Varma sits cross-legged on a mat.
- **10.2, after the page turn:** Varma sits cross-legged on a red cushion on a low dais.

The script's hall plan says Varma sits on a "slightly raised wooden platform" and Ramayyan's "low table is at the king's left hand", and 9.5 repeats this ("on the platform above him"). Nothing in the script or bible allows a chair or throne. Seating the diwan on a throne equal to the king's also flattens the king-minister hierarchy the chapter builds.

It is not too slight to matter: the thrones are large, lit and central in a full-width panel. I rate it major, not blocker. It is a localized set and staging error; both figures are still recognizable, and the beat and lettering read correctly. The panel's other elements are fine: Nagoji is on a mat, both men are on a raised area, Varma's turban and crest are right, and Ramayyan wears plain white.

verdict.reason:
I'm confirming this as major, though only one of its two parts holds up at that level. I zoomed into page 5, panel 5.4 at full resolution.

1) The "You mistrust pilots?" tail is a real attribution problem. It runs into the top-left corner of the panel. The only figure there is a blurred foreground figure: cream cloth with a gold patterned border along the left edge and a bare brown shoulder below it. That figure's head would sit in the same top-left area the tail points at. The look matches Varma's court costume: bare chest and cream-and-gold cloth, as in 5.3 and 5.5 and on the varma-v1 sheet. Ramayyan wears plain white cloth that covers his shoulders, with no gold. The panel is a reverse angle from the platform, so readers will take that foreground figure for the king. The script says Varma's only lettered word in the chapter is "Ram." Its end note also names "You mistrust pilots?" arriving off panel in 5.4 as a planned beat that shows the king is ahead of his interpreter. Pointing the tail at a figure that reads as Varma undercuts both. The cast list for 5.4 has only Nagoji, so the foreground figure was never planned. This is a localized fix: move the tail off the top edge or the left edge mid-height, away from the figure, without redrawing the art.

2) The "I mistrust everyone who touches a coin." part is smaller than reported. The tail tip does end on the right edge of the standing guard's red sash, about 230 px at full resolution (roughly 0.75 in at print) left of Nagoji's mouth. But it points straight at Nagoji's shoulder, only about 50 px from his shirt. The guard is a background figure with his mouth shut, and his head is far above the tip. Nagoji's open mouth, gesturing hand and next balloon all tie the line to him. On its own this is minor: extend the tail toward his mouth.

Taken together, two of the three tails in this panel point wrong, and one goes against the chapter's lettering rule for Varma. That is a wrong speaker tail, which the severity guide lists as major. It is not a blocker, since it needs no redraw.

confirmed.description: The framing differs from the script and the king's seating changes. The script asks for a high shot from the entrance end, with Nagoji small on his mat below the king and diwan on the platform. The art is a low, near-level side view. Nagoji kneels large at the left, and Varma and Ramayyan sit on tall carved throne chairs with red cushions. In every other panel of the chapter Varma sits cross-legged on a mat on the platform.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed on page 9, panel 9.5, based on a crop of the panel at full resolution.

What the art shows:
- **Seating:** Varma sits upright on a tall, dark carved throne chair with red cushions. Ramayyan sits on a matching carved chair beside him. There is no low table for Ramayyan.
- **Camera:** The view is low and close to level, not high from the entrance end. Nagoji kneels on a rug at the far left and fills about half the panel's height. The script asks for him to be "small on his mat".

Why the seating change is a real error:
- **Script:** The script places Varma on a mat in several panels. At 2.2 a map lies "on the mat before him". At 8.5 he taps his spear butt "against the mat". At 10.2 Ramayyan says the king "has spent too many lives to sit on that mat".
- **Script, Ramayyan:** He is fixed at "his low table" throughout the scene. Seating him on a throne-style chair level with the king breaks that plan.
- **Other pages:** Every other platform shot in this render set (pages 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 and 10) shows Varma seated cross-legged on the low platform or dais.
- **Next page:** The throne appears for one panel only. Page 10, panel 10.2 goes straight back to Varma seated low beside Ramayyan, against the "that mat" line. The furniture visibly jumps within the same audience.
- **Not allowed elsewhere:** Neither CONTINUITY.md nor the cast overrides permits a throne. The chapter's own "They did not take me to a palace" contrast works against one.

Why major and not blocker:
- Both faces and costumes are correct: Varma has the cream-and-gold turban with crest, and Ramayyan the plain white cloth.
- The open side of the hall is on screen left, as the script asks.
- The verdict beat still reads, with Nagoji kneeling below the raised king and diwan.
- The lettering is legible.

So the problem is localized: a furniture and framing continuity error that is clearly visible at print size. Redraw the panel with both men seated on the mat-covered platform, Ramayyan at his low table, and a higher shot from the entrance end so Nagoji reads smaller.

And his diwan.") stops on the crown of Nagoji's hair, just short of the left edge of Ibrahim's turban. The tail of the lower balloon ("Remember what I said about gifts.") stops on Nagoji's shoulder, behind his neck, beside Ibrahim's beard. Neither tip reaches Ibrahim's mouth. Ibrahim's lips are parted while Nagoji's are closed. The lines themselves (the mentor naming the court, then "Remember what I said") fit only Ibrahim, as the script directs. confirmed.description: Ramayyan's introduction panel crops his head at the brow line. His identifying receding hair is lost, and with dense curls showing at the top he reads younger and different from the balding diwan in 2.2 and on pages 3 to 10. The production notes say this frame becomes his reference for later panels. confirmed.evidence: The top panel border cuts across his forehead just above the eyebrows. Compare 9.3, where his bald crown and curly sides are clear. Behind him on the left are moored ships, crates and standing men on a waterfront.

verdict.reason:
I confirm the head-crop problem. It is major, not a blocker, and a recrop fixes it without a redraw.

**What I checked**
- **The panel at 300 DPI:** In page 2, panel 2.4, the top panel border cuts across Ramayyan's forehead just above his eyebrows (about y≈1600 on the 1838x2775 page). Only curls at his temples and sides show. His bald crown is gone.
- **The source frame** (chapters/ch06/frames/page-02-panel-04-v01.png): it draws him correctly, with a clearly bald crown and curly sides that match the approved sheet 03-ramayyan-dalawa-v15.png, which has a dedicated HAIRLINE detail. The art is right; the page layout's fitted crop (LAYOUT-fitted) removed the feature.
- **Why it matters:** The script for 2.4 asks for "receding hair", and so does Ramayyan's CONTINUITY base line. 2.4 is his introduction. Production note line 372 makes this frame his reference for later panels. 2.2, 9.2, 9.3 and 9.5 all show the bald crown. With it cropped away, the close-up reads younger and less clearly as the same diwan.
- **Why not a blocker:** The caption names him, and his face, white cloth, palm-leaf table and stylus all match the sheet. The source frame has enough headroom above him, so the fix is to recrop 2.4 lower so the crown sits inside the border. 9.1 has a similar tight crop at the top of his head; it is less important because he is already established by then.

**The setting part of the report is weak.** The hall plan puts the open side with the sea on screen left, and 9.1 and 9.4 also show ships, the fort and the shore. The pillar, guards, conch banner and lamp on the right keep 2.4 inside the hall. The ground-level quay with crates and walking men is at most a minor mismatch with the raised view in 2.1, not a major problem on its own.

confirmed.description: Both captions point at 'that horizon', but the two caption boxes cover almost all of it. confirmed.evidence: The left caption ('Somewhere beyond that horizon...') and the right caption ('Somewhere farther still...') cover the sky and the horizon line on both sides. verdict.reason:
I'm confirming this one. At full resolution, panel 7.5 shows what the reviewer described.

1. **The captions hide the horizon.** The horizon sits about 100 px below the top of the panel. The left caption reaches about 137 px down and the right one about 178 px, so both run below the horizon. Sea meeting sky shows only in a gap of roughly 120 px in a panel about 1540 px wide (under 10%), and that gap holds a mast and a small rock. The script asks for "a hard, empty horizon" with "the sky open for two captions". The page is meant to end on the horizon, but both "that horizon" captions sit over it.

2. **There is no height.** The hall's stone floor runs straight out to the sand at eye level. The men loading sacks and nets are mid-sized figures, not "small as ants". The script asks for "the inlet below". Panel 1.3 puts the hall "on the rise beyond" a red stone outer wall, and 2.1 says "through it, below, the sea".

3. **It contradicts panel 7.3 on the same page.** In 7.3 the king gestures down from the hall at an inlet with moored boats and red stone walls well below. Panel 7.5 is meant to show that same view, but it puts the hall at beach level with no wall and no inlet. A reader sees two different places only a few inches apart.

The lettering is readable and the sea, boats and workers are there, so the beat is not lost. That keeps this from being a blocker. It is still a clear, localized staging and composition error, so major is the right severity.

refuted.description: Ramayyan's identity is wrong in his introduction close-up. He is drawn with a full head of thick curly black hair down to the brow, with no receding hairline. The approved sheet (03-ramayyan-dalawa-v15.png) and the bible line ('receding hair') call for a bald crown with curls only at the sides and back. Every later Ramayyan panel follows the sheet (3.1, 4.2, 5.3, 6.2, 9.1, 9.3, 10.3), so the man named by the 'Ramayyan' caption does not match the diwan for the rest of the chapter. The script's production notes also make this frame the reference for all of his later panels, so the drift would spread.
refuted.reason: The art doesn't show the problem. In panel 2.4 on page 2, the panel's top border cuts Ramayyan's head off at the eyebrows (about y 1605 in the 1838x2775 render). His forehead and crown are out of frame, so the panel shows neither a low hairline nor curly hair across the crown. In a 8x zoom of the strip just below the border, the brows run straight into the border line with skin between them. Dark curly hair shows only at the sides, by the temples and above the ears. The approved sheet (03-ramayyan-dalawa-v15.png) also has hair at that level, so this fits the "curls at sides and back" design. The face also matches the sheet: thin, sharp fine features, plain white cloth wrapped over the upper body, no jewellery, with stylus, palm-leaf bundles and ink pot. Nothing on the page contradicts the bible's "receding hair". The receding crown just isn't visible here. At most, the tight crop hides his signature bald crown in his first close-up, which is a composition note, not a wrong identity.

refuted.description: Both of Ibrahim's balloon tails end on Nagoji, not on Ibrahim. The tail of 'Marthanda Varma. And his diwan.' stops in Nagoji's hair, and the tail of 'Remember what I said about gifts.' stops on Nagoji's shirt below his ear. As drawn, Nagoji appears to say both lines.
refuted.reason: Refuted as a wrong-speaker problem. At most it is a minor polish note. On the full-resolution crop of page 2, panel 2.3 (page-02.png, 1838x2775), both tips do stop on Nagoji. The upper tip is at about (1347,1177), in the curls at the back of his head, just left of the lower edge of Ibrahim's turban. The lower tip is at about (1365,1297), on his collar under his back hair, roughly 35 px from Ibrahim's beard. But both tails point at Ibrahim. The upper tail runs from about (1290,1115) at the balloon to the tip. Extended, it reaches about (1400,1240), which is Ibrahim's moustache and mouth at about (1405-1420,1235). The lower tail runs from about (1315,1370) to the tip. Extended, it also reaches about (1404,1240). So the two tails meet on Ibrahim's mouth. Neither one goes near Nagoji's mouth at about (1240,1260). Nagoji is in profile facing left toward the balloons, and both tails pass his face and end behind his head and neck. That is not where a tail would go if he were speaking. At print size the panel is about 2.5 in wide and each tip is only about 6-7 mm short. Both tips sit on the seam where the two heads touch, and Ibrahim is clearly leaning in to whisper with his lips parted, as script 2.3 asks ('Ibrahim at Nagoji's ear, lips barely moving'). Context also gives the lines to Ibrahim. Nagoji's voice on this page is only in the captions, and 'Remember what I said about gifts' calls back to Ibrahim's own earlier advice. The chapter's earlier review used the same standard for the 9.5 tail (refuted there): a tail is read by where it points, and a tip that falls a little short is polish. Optional fix: extend each tip about 70-85 px along its own angle so it ends on Ibrahim's beard or mouth.

refuted.description: The off-panel balloon 'They questioned you.' (Ramayyan) sits in the gap between Varma's two extended fingers and Nagoji's bandaged hands, which breaks the gesture's line. Its tail points back up toward Varma's arm, so the Konkani line reads as the king's. That undoes the chapter's device that Varma's only lettered word is 'Ram.'
refuted.reason: I checked page 3, panel 3.5 at full resolution, and the major claim does not hold up. (1) The tail does not point "just above the bangled forearm." Its tip ends on the top border at about x=917 px (page coordinates). That is roughly 150 to 170 px (about 0.5 in at 300 DPI) right of where the forearm leaves the top border (about x=550 to 760), above the brass lamp and wall. It never touches or aims at the arm. A tail running to the border is the standard off-panel convention, and up and slightly left is a reasonable direction for Ramayyan, who sits at the platform's front corner beside the king. (2) The gesture line is not broken. The lower extended finger, the one that points, is fully visible, and the open space from its tip down and right to Nagoji's bandaged hands is clear wall background, below the balloon. (3) The context settles who is speaking. On this same page, 3.3 sets up the convention that Varma speaks only through the "[in Malayalam]" tag, and 3.4 runs Ramayyan question, Nagoji answer, twice. 3.5 continues that rhythm directly, so readers will take "They questioned you." as Ramayyan's. The script also has the king's gesture prompt the diwan's line, so a loose link between the hand and the line is in keeping with the scene. It does not undo the rule that Varma's only lettered word is "Ram." What remains true is minor polish. The balloon's left edge covers the tip of the upper of the two extended fingers, a tangency that slightly crowds the hand. Nudging the balloon about 30 to 40 px right or up would fix it. This does not justify a major rating or a redraw.

minors.description: The present-day Nagoji seated at the lower left of the memory panel has no gold ear stud. Every other present-day Nagoji in the chapter wears one, and it is part of the bible's constant identity line.
minors.evidence: In page-08.png, crop x 440-640, y 1170-1340: his ear on screen left is clearly drawn and bare, and the other ear is hidden by hair. Compare 8.1 and 8.4 on the same page, where the gold ornament is visible.

minors.description: Nagoji, kneeling on his mat in profile, has a bare ear with no gold stud. He is facing screen right, so his visible ear is the one that carries the ornament in the other profiles (8.4, 10.5).
minors.evidence: In page-09.png, crop x 290-440, y 2140-2290: a clear profile with the ear fully exposed above the tied-back hair, and no gold on it.

minors.description: Across the whole chapter, Nagoji's ear ornament is drawn as a hanging gold drop (the nagoji-v2 sheet's version), not the small flush gold stud the bible requires. Per the author's 2026-10-02 decision, this is the known ch1-8 deviation, to be listed for the author and not reopened automatically. It is recorded here so that list includes ch6.
minors.evidence: The drop earring hangs below the lobe in 1.2, 1.4, 1.5, 2.3, 4.3, 5.1, 5.2, 5.4, 6.3, 8.1, 8.4, 10.1, 10.3 and 10.5 (for example, page-01.png crop x 300-480, y 840-1000, and page-06.png crop x 580-800, y 1500-1720). Otherwise Nagoji is consistent throughout: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with light stubble at most, long curly black hair, no beard.

minors.description: Varma's turban has drifted to salmon and peach banding instead of the cream-and-gold of the varma-v1 sheet and of every other Varma panel in the chapter. His face, Vaishnavite mark, pearl earrings and crest otherwise match.
minors.evidence: In page-10.png, crop x 940-1140, y 450-680: the wraps of the turban show pink and peach stripes. Compare the cream-and-gold turban in 9.2 (page-09.png, x 360-520, y 820-980) and 7.4.

minors.description: Nagoji's shirt reads as captivity rags here. It is visibly stained, with a ragged, frayed hem and a torn neckline. In every other present-day panel (3.1, 4.2, 5.4, 6.3, 10.1) he wears a clean, plain cream shirt, which matches the ch6 row ('simple cream shirt').
minors.evidence: Crop of page-03 at x 1300-1560, y 1800-2170: brown blotches over the shirt, a shredded lower edge and a frayed V-neck.

minors.description: The view through the open side of the hall changes. In 3.1 and 3.3 the open side (screen left, as the plan says) shows a towered hilltop fortress over palms and no sea. On page 2 (2.1, 2.2), and later on page 6 (6.1) and page 7 (7.3), the same side looks onto the sea and the inlet, as the hall plan and 1.3 require. Page 4, panel 4.2 repeats the hill-fort view on the reverse angle.
minors.evidence: Page-03 at x 150-500, y 1145-1500 (3.3) and at x 150-600, y 355-700 (3.1): sandstone towers on a wooded hill, no water. Page-04 panel 4.2, upper right: the same hill citadel.

minors.description: The top panel border crops Varma's turban at the brow, so the jewelled peacock-feather crest and the Vaishnavite forehead mark are both lost. The script's visual lock asks for the crest in every panel of this audience.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-05 at x 500-900, y 2030-2140: only the lower band of a plain cream turban shows above the eyebrows, with no crest, feather or namam.

minors.description: The map has moved. On page 2 it lies open on the mat before Varma on the low platform (2.2). Here, and at 4.5, it lies on a raised wooden writing table that Varma leans over, with Ramayyan's palm-leaf bundles on the same tabletop. His 'low table' has become a shared desk.
minors.evidence: Page-05 panel 5.3 (x 920-1690, y 765-1585): the map and the brass ink pot sit on a high dark wooden table. Page-02 panel 2.2: the map is unrolled on the floor mat next to the sword.

minors.description: The background guards' uniform changes within the page. In 6.4 they wear rust-red turbans, red waist sashes and red crossed belts over white tunics. In 6.1 and 6.3 the guards are bare-headed with topknots, wearing black sashes and plain crossed leather belts. Red turban with red sash is also Nagoji's own commander signature from chapter 7 onward, so these extras will echo it. The same switch happens on page 5 (5.5 against 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4) and appears again in 9.2.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-06 at x 205-800, y 2180-2450: three guards in red turbans and red sashes. Page-06 panel 6.3 background: a bare-chested guard with a black sash and no turban.

minors.description: In this wide, mostly empty panel, the top border crops Varma's head at the brow. The turban reads as a thin cream band, with no jewelled peacock-feather crest and no forehead lines. There is plenty of room to drop him into frame.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-08 at x 680-900, y 2200-2300: the panel border cuts across the turban just above the eyebrows. Only an edge of the gold band shows.

minors.description: In profile, Varma's turban shows no jewelled peacock-feather crest. The front of the turban, where the crest sits, is cropped by the top border, so the turban reads as a plain cream wrap.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-09 at x 180-700, y 1330-1700: a cream turban with a gold band and a pearl earring, with no crest, feather or jewel anywhere in frame.

minors.description: The view through the open side shows a Portuguese-looking town: a whitewashed church bell tower and arcaded villas with red-tile roofs. It reads as Goa rather than the Travancore inlet, boats and red laterite walls established at 1.3 and 7.3. A similar European-style villa appears behind Ibrahim at 1.4.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-09 at x 150-300, y 1040-1260: a bell tower and colonnaded Mediterranean houses among palms. Page-07 panel 7.3 shows only red stone walls and moored boats through the same opening.

minors.description: The Travancore guards here wear red turbans, white tunics and trousers, crossed red-brown shoulder belts and red waistbands. That reads as a later British-Indian (East India Company) sepoy uniform rather than 1740s Nair guards. It also clashes with the page 1 guards, who are bare-chested in white cotton with dark sashes as the script specifies. The same white tunic and crossbelt guard shows in the backgrounds of 3.3, 4.2 and 6.1.
minors.evidence: Three guards stand around Ibrahim in 6.4: one at far left, one behind him and one between the pillars. Each has a red turban, a white uniform, crossed belts and a red waistband. In 3.3 a guard in a white turban and white tunic with crossed brown belts and a red sash stands behind Varma's shoulder.

minors.description: The view through the open side shows what reads as a European colonial town, closer to Portuguese Goa than the Travancore coast below the fort.
minors.evidence: At the left edge, behind Varma, there is a church bell tower with a red pointed top above a cluster of whitewashed villas with red-tiled roofs and arcades. Similar whitewashed, red-roofed buildings sit on the outer wall in 7.3 (upper left), and a white domed tower shows through the pillars in 2.2.

minors.description: Ramayyan's first translation balloon ('He says they already have horse from the Nayak of Madurai...') sits right under Varma's face, across his chest. Its short tail only reaches Ramayyan's sleeve, so a reader could take it as Varma's line.
minors.evidence: The balloon body covers Varma's torso from the necklaces down. The tail tip stops on Ramayyan's upper arm, about 180 px (full resolution) from his mouth.

minors.description: Ramayyan's second balloon covers his whole body and the end of his outstretched arm. The scripted beat of Ramayyan pointing his stylus at the mat is hidden. The balloon also sits flush against the panel's left border.
minors.evidence: Only Ramayyan's head, shoulder and the start of his arm show. The balloon fills the lower-left half of the panel, from the left frame line to the edge of the mat.

minors.description: The inset is crowded. Nagoji's off-panel balloon lies over the inset's right edge and frame line, and Ramayyan's balloon lies over its bottom edge. Nagoji's long tail runs down through the panel onto the map. The Varma [in Malayalam] tag (right) and Ramayyan's translation (bottom-left) are almost level, so a reader may read the translation before the king's line.
minors.evidence: The inset frame (top-left) is cut by the left third of the 'And their infantry...' balloon. The tail runs from that balloon to the bottom border at the map's river area. Ramayyan's balloon begins just under the Malayalam balloon's bottom edge, but on the far side of the panel.

minors.description: Ibrahim's second balloon ('He comes from Portuguese chains...') covers Nagoji's bowing body from the chest down, including his bandaged hands, plus the front of the platform and map. The bow is the panel's action. The first balloon sits flush against the left frame line.
minors.evidence: In the crop, only Nagoji's head and back show above the balloon. The left balloon's outer edge touches the panel's left border.

minors.description: In this short strip, the two balloons take up most of the panel. Nagoji's head is cut by the top border, and his bandaged hands on his knees are partly hidden by the right balloon. The beat of his eyes coming back to the king is cramped.
minors.evidence: The top of Nagoji's hair is cut by the frame. The right balloon covers his lap and one bandaged hand.

minors.description: The panel's top border crops off Varma's turban and peacock-feather crest. Only the lower band of the turban shows above his face, so the required headwear does not read on the 'Ram.' beat. Page 9, panel 4 has the same crop: Varma's turban is cut and no crest shows.
minors.evidence: 8.5: Varma's head is pressed against the top frame line, with only the turban rim visible. 9.4: The turban is cut at the top-left and has no crest.

minors.description: Throughout the chapter, the '[in Malayalam]' tag is set in upright roman type. The script's lettering convention calls for 'a small balloon holding only that italic tag'. Voice qualifiers are also left unlettered: 1.3 Ibrahim '(small, soft)' is a full-size balloon, 5.3 Varma '(sharp)' is a plain smooth balloon, and 5.5 Ramayyan '(soft)' is a normal balloon.
minors.evidence: '[in Malayalam]' is upright in 3.3, 4.5, 5.3, 6.1, 6.4, 7.3, 9.2, 9.4 and 10.2, while the 10.4 vow captions are clearly italic. The 1.3 'This is only one claw' balloon is the same size and weight as the other dialogue.

minors.description: Several balloons sit flush against or touch the panel borders, with none of the inner margin used in the approved Chapter 1. Here, Nagoji's two balloons touch the left border, the right border and nearly the bottom border. The same happens in 9.1 (left balloon jammed into the top-left corner, right balloon on the top border), 10.2 (third balloon on the right border), 10.3 (balloon on the left border) and 6.3 ('Any war...' balloon on the left border).
minors.evidence: In each crop, the balloon's outer stroke meets the panel frame line with no gap.

minors.description: The chapter's closing caption is a standard box placed tight against Nagoji's head, in the eyeline of his look up the coast. The script asks for it to be separate and weighted. Nagoji's head is also cropped by the top border.
minors.evidence: The caption's left edge is a few pixels from Nagoji's face. The top of his hair is cut by the frame. The caption uses the same style as every other narration box.

minors.description: Widowed single words at the ends of text blocks: 'it.' alone on the last line of 'He has spent too many lives...' (10.2), and 'stone.' alone in the 10.4 vow caption.
minors.evidence: 10.2: the final line of the bottom-right balloon is just 'it.' 10.4: the bottom-left italic caption ends on a one-word line, 'stone.'

minors.description: The panel's top border cuts through Nagoji's head, from his hairline up. In the closing strip of the page, his face is crammed against the frame beside the caption. Ramayyan's head is cropped the same way in 2.4, and in 9.1 with balloons hugging him.
minors.evidence: In 1.5, Nagoji's eyes sit just below the frame line and the top of his head is cut off. In 2.4, the top of Ramayyan's hair is cut by the frame.

minors.description: The gate guards do not match the script. The script asks for Travancore guards in white cotton with dark sashes, carrying matchlocks and spears. The art shows bare-chested guards with leather crossbelts and only spears. A whitewashed, European-looking two-storey house with a red tile roof also stands behind the gate, which is not in the script.
minors.evidence: The greeting guard and his neighbours are shirtless, with brown leather straps across the chest. No matchlocks are visible. The white building sits in the centre background behind Ibrahim's turban.

minors.description: The script makes 1.3 the largest panel on the page, but it is the same size as 1.2, and 1.4 is larger. Ibrahim's '(small, soft)' line is lettered in a full-size balloon.
minors.evidence: 1.2 and 1.3 are equal half-width panels in the same row. 1.4 below is wider and of similar height. The 'This is only one claw...' balloon uses the same size and font as normal dialogue.

minors.description: The king's reveal is staged as a medium shot on the platform, not as a large shot 'down the clear lane to the far end'. Ramayyan is well lit and fairly prominent, not 'small and in shadow'. The panel is the same size as 2.3, not large.
minors.evidence: Varma fills most of the half-width panel at close-medium range. Ramayyan sits at his table on the right in even light.

minors.description: The script's entry staging is weak. There is no 'top of a short flight of stone steps' viewpoint, and the seated men run down the centre instead of leaving a clear lane to the platform.
minors.evidence: The camera is at floor level on the verandah. The rows of seated men line up straight toward the platform in the middle of the frame, ahead of Nagoji and Ibrahim.

minors.description: The script has Nagoji 'seated on the mat, talking, one bandaged hand shaping a low wall in the air'. The panel crops him at the chest, so both the hand gesture and the mat are out of frame.
minors.evidence: Only Nagoji's head and shoulders show at the bottom centre. No hands are visible.

minors.description: This breaks the hall plan for platform two-shots, which puts the open side on screen left. Here the sea and palms show through a balustrade directly behind the pair, mostly behind Ramayyan at centre right.
minors.evidence: The open sea view sits between Varma's shoulder and Ramayyan's head. Screen left behind Varma is plain sky with no pillars or open side.

minors.description: The top panel border crops off Varma's turban crest. The script's visual lock calls for the cream-and-gold turban with its jewelled peacock-feather crest in every panel. The same crop happens at 5.5.
minors.evidence: In 8.5 the top border cuts the turban just above his brow, so no feather or jewel shows. In 5.5 only the lower band of the turban is in frame.

minors.description: The top-left border crops off Varma's turban crest, so the peacock-feather crest locked in the script is missing.
minors.evidence: Only the lower wrap of the turban shows at the top-left corner, with no feather or jewel.
